meta.question: Why did our website slow down on Black Friday?
meta.title: Black Friday slowdown, 28/11/2025
meta.author: Platform team, Thistle & Thread (fictional)
meta.footer: Fictional company and data, for illustration only.

answer.headline: The product database ran out of connections: a new 'recently viewed' feature made each page open four database queries instead of one, so at four times normal traffic requests queued and pages took up to 9 seconds.
answer.text: Servers, network and the content delivery network all had spare capacity. The bottleneck was a fixed pool of 200 database connections shared by every web server, which the new feature quietly used up.
points: Slow from 08:55 to 10:40; pages took a median of 4.2 seconds at the worst point
Adding web servers made it worse: each new server added more queries to the same pool
Turning off 'recently viewed' at 10:32 fixed it within eight minutes

blocks.title: Traffic and page time on the morning
blocks.caption: Page time jumped once traffic passed about 4,000 visitors a minute, and recovered after 10:40 although traffic stayed high.

blocks.title: Where the requests queued
blocks.caption: Step 3 of the walkthrough: every web server draws from one connection pool.

meta.title: Product page request path
meta.description: A product page goes through the CDN to a web server, which reads from the product database through a shared connection pool.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: The request path for one product page.

steps.title: Edge is fine
steps.description: The CDN served images and scripts with plenty of headroom.

steps.title: Queue at the pool
steps.description: Each page now held four connections. At peak, requests waited for a free connection.

steps.title: Database had room
steps.description: The database itself was at 45% CPU: it was never the limit.

items.title: Web servers scaled from 8 to 20
items.text: Page time gets worse, not better.

items.title: Connection pool identified
items.text: Database dashboards show all 200 connections in use.

items.title: Feature switched off
items.text: Using its feature flag; no deploy needed.

blocks.title: Why it was hard to spot

items.title: The usual signs were green
items.text: CPU and memory looked healthy everywhere.

items.title: Scaling hid the cause
items.text: More servers is the normal fix for slowness, and here it made the queue longer.

items.title: No pool alert
items.text: We measured database CPU, not waiting for connections.
Load 'recently viewed' in one query, from a cache
Alert when the connection pool is over 80% in use
Load-test at five times normal traffic before peak events
Add a connection proxy so the pool size does not grow with server count

items.a: Orders still went through, but about 18% fewer than forecast for those two hours. Most of that demand returned later in the day.

items.q: Why not just make the pool bigger?
items.a: Each connection uses memory on the database. A proxy that shares connections between servers fixes the cause instead of moving the limit.
